name: Ngarla on the Ashburton river south of the Hamersley range

earlier_scan.note: Retired/bookkeeping Glottolog entry (split into nrk/ywg); only O'Grady et al. 1966 name it; no stress description located

readall_conflicts: No stress statements were found, so no conflict about stress. There is an identity conflict between databases: Austlang W40 (coastal Ngarla, De Grey River, ISO nlr) lists Glottocode ngar1286, whereas Glottolog's own label for ngar1286 is 'Ngarla on the Ashburton river south of the Hamersley range', i.e. the inland A48/Ngarlawangga/Yinhawangka referent; Austlang A48 itself says it is 'not to be confused with Ngarla W40' and records the A48/A79 code swap with Yinhawangka. Any stress claim attached to ngar1286 would therefore have to be routed either to coastal Ngarla (ngar1296, already catalogued from Westerlund 2015 as initial stress) or to Yinhawangka (yinh1234), for which no stress description has been located.

sources.citation: Westerlund, Torbjörn. 2015. A grammatical sketch of Ngarla (Ngayarta, Pama-Nyungan). Asia-Pacific Linguistics A-PL 16. Canberra: ANU. 186 pp. (hdl 1885/14712)

sources.note: COASTAL Ngarla (nrk = ngar1296, De Grey River/Port Hedland), sec. 2.3 p.10: 'Stress in Ngarla is predictable.. According to Geytenbeek (2006), the stress placement rules of Ngarla are as shown in Table 7' = main stress on 1st syllable; secondary on 3rd (4-syll), 4th (5-syll), 3rd+5th (6-syll); suffixes -kujarra, -rukarra, -pungkara carry their own main stress on their second syllable. pp.1-2: the names Ngalawanga/Ngalawarngga/Ngalawonga 'in fact usually designate a community with another language' that 'traditionally lived on the upper Ashburton river.. neighbouring the Panyjima, Wawula, Watj…

sources.note: COASTAL Ngarla: 'As a primary rule stress should be placed on the first syllable of each word.. In words of four or five syllables, the second-to-last syllable is also stressed, though more lightly than the first.' plus a vowel-elision exception (kuwarri -> 'kwa:rri') with stress shifting to the next vowel.
